name: Project Charter
one_liner: The what, how and when — approved by the PSC before planning starts.
purpose: The Project Charter provides the basis for more detailed project planning. It defines the project's objectives in scope, time, cost and quality, its high-level requirements, risks and constraints, and its milestones and deliverables. Together with the Business Case it is the key element of the project approval process: it holds the what, how and when fundamentals and gives a baseline against which progress can be measured.
approved_by: Project Steering Committee (PSC) accepts it; the Appropriate Governance Body (AGB) gives corporate-level approval where needed

lifecycle.what: PM completes it from the Business Case; PSC accepts at RfP
Baseline for Handbook, Work Plan and the management plans
Changed only through approved Change Requests; deviations escalate
Scope and criteria compared against actuals in the Project-End Report

fields.what: An executive summary of the whole charter; the template says explicitly to complete this section last.
fields.castor: A 26-month, €8.4 m programme to replace LOS with a configurable lending operations platform, delivered as a Mix.

fields.what: Pertinent considerations on the approved Business Case; revisit impact and urgency, and validate external influences, interfaces and regulatory requirements.
fields.castor: Urgency confirmed: the backstop must be onboardable within weeks of Treaty reform, which LOS cannot support.

fields.what: The outputs the project WILL deliver, forming the solution; may include the organisational change management activities needed to realise the benefits.
fields.who: PM drafts · PO agrees · PSC approves
fields.castor: Product configuration engine, straight-through disbursement, same-day reconciliation, audit trail, retraining of 40 loan administrators.

fields.what: What the project will NOT deliver — as important as the IN scope for managing expectations, including things discussed and then excluded.
fields.castor: Replacement of the treasury system or payment messaging gateway; SRF-backstop screens beyond configurable product set-up.

fields.what: An overall scope statement in one or two lines, complete enough for management and outsiders to understand the project.
fields.castor: Replace LOS with a configurable platform giving straight-through processing from loan agreement to disbursement and repayment.

fields.what: Measurable criteria by which the project is judged a success or failure; separate product success criteria from overall project criteria.
fields.castor: SC1 5→1 working day; SC2 3 days→same day; SC3 9 months→6 weeks; SC4 1,400 fields→0; SC5 2 findings→0

fields.what: Table of key needs — ID, description, priority — answering who has the need, what it is, why it must be met and how it is met today.
fields.castor: N-01 Loan administrators: enter a disbursement instruction once (priority: must). N-02 Risk: complete audit trail.

fields.what: Table of project outputs — ID, name, description; standard PM² artefacts are explicitly excluded from this list.
fields.castor: D-01 product configuration engine · D-02 straight-through disbursement · D-03 reconciliation reporting · D-04 trained users

fields.what: High-level capabilities of the outputs, aligned to the needs: Related Need, Features, Deliverable(s). Focus on what and why, not how.
fields.castor: N-01 → single-entry instruction with maker-checker → D-02; N-02 → immutable event log per instruction → D-03

fields.what: Constraints on people, schedule, budget, resources, products, technology and interfaces, plus decisions, compliance, security, document management and data protection.
fields.who: PM drafts · SP and PO confirm
fields.castor: €8.4 m and 26 months; no disruption to live disbursements; parallel run must fit the 2028 bond-rollover calendar.

fields.what: Assumptions on business, technology, resources, environment, scope, expectations or schedules — facts still to be validated, or they become risks.
fields.castor: All ESM instruments expressible by configuration; business experts available part-time throughout the parallel run.

fields.what: Key risks at this initial stage with response strategies, in log format; does not replace the full Planning-phase risk assessment.
fields.who: PM owns log · PO owns business risk
fields.castor: R-07 loss of the contractor's key architect — High/High — Mitigate: named-staff clause and knowledge transfer.

fields.what: Financing structure: expenditure lines, budget lines, amounts per year, total cost and FTE of internal staff, plus the delivered solution's TCO.
fields.castor: €8.4 m over 2026–2028 across solution development, infrastructure, support and training; 3,100 PD internal effort.

fields.what: Important points in time: ID, milestone description, target delivery date, including the timing of the PM² phases and management deliverables.
fields.castor: M-01 RfE 03 Jul 2026 · M-02 contract award 18 Sep 2026 · M-03 R1 26 Mar 2027 · M-05 go-live 15 May 2028

fields.what: Numbers and types of staff by phase with special skills, how they will be acquired, and non-human resources with the role responsible for providing them.
fields.who: SP and BM supply · PM records
fields.castor: Core team of 9 from IT & Digital plus contractor staff; 4 business experts part-time from Lending Operations.

fields.what: The chosen project management methodology and any deviations from it, plus the chosen domain-specific methodology (e.g. for IS development).
fields.castor: PM² with no deviations; platform implementation delivered in two releases by the integrator.

fields.what: The adopted project change management process; changes to the content of this document are subject to formal approval.
fields.castor: Change Request Form → Change Log → PSC decision; verbal scope requests are not actioned.

fields.what: Creation, maintenance and controlled change of project items; which items may only change with authorisation, and by which process.
fields.castor: Scope, budget, milestone dates and baselined artefacts change only by PSC decision; Johannes Gutenberg (DMO) holds the repository.

fields.what: Organisational change goals and activities to take into account — elaborated later in the Business Implementation Plan.
fields.castor: Retraining of 40 loan administrators and new maker-checker roles; detailed in the Business Implementation Plan.

fields.what: The organisational structure of the project team and stakeholders, preferably as a diagram, referencing the PM² definition of the PSC.
fields.castor: PSC chaired by Florence Nightingale: PO, SP Leonardo da Vinci, BM Grace Hopper, PM, plus UR, AO and CPM.

fields.what: The roles and responsibilities of project governance — the standard PM² assignment, plus any deviations from it.
fields.castor: Standard PM² roles; optional PSC members: Marie Curie (UR), Albert Einstein (AO), Gustave Eiffel (CPM).

fields.what: All project stakeholders with a brief profile of the key ones and the problems they expect the solution to address — background, not requirements.
fields.castor: Finance & Control, Risk, Legal, Internal Audit, Project Support Team (PQA, PSO, DPC, LISO, DMO).

fields.what: Each reference by title, version, date and source or location, plus the project folder; the Business Case is the first entry.
fields.castor: 02.Business_Case.CASTOR.24-03-2026.V1.0.docx; CASTOR project folder

traps: The PSC is Accountable and the PM Responsible — the PO is only Consulted (C).
The BM may start it, but the PM completes it and submits it for approval.
Charter = what, how, when. Why and the option analysis stay in the Business Case.
No detailed requirements here — high-level needs and features only.
If the Charter is rejected the project goes straight to Closing for lessons learned.
